context:
Goal: more places where an agent argues back, beyond hooks, review and plans (your note on item 279).
Problem (money): each option adds about one Sonnet call every time it is used.
Based on (measured): an Opus audit at 12:57 CST of every verdict that lands with no agent arguing back. Its top finding is that a lane's own claims decide how much review it gets. Two fixes for that need no model call, and they are already being built.
Based on (ruling): your picks a, b and d on item 279.
Departs from: main, where the asking session alone writes a question's pick and why, a pick skipped because a ruling covers it goes unchecked, and a brief's done-check line goes unchecked — adds a blind reader for each one you tick.
lane: coordinator: steps challenger-page-against, ruling-skip-check, check-line-reader; routed 13:12 CST

lastAnswer.note: Owner: some challengers should run Opus, not all Sonnet, and there are probably more places to use them. Routed 13:12 CST to the coordinator.

options.gain: You see the strongest argument against the recommendation before you pick.
options.how: On each page question, a blind Sonnet writes the best case for the strongest option that isn't recommended.
options.label: Best case against the pick

options.gain: A ruling can't be stretched to cover something you never ruled on.
options.how: When a session skips asking you because a ruling covers it, it cites the ruling and its time, and a Sonnet confirms that the ruling names that exact act.
options.label: Check ruling-based skips

options.gain: Work can't be marked done by a check that misses the point.
options.how: A blind Sonnet reads only a brief's ask and its done-check line, and flags a check that could pass with the ask unmet. It reads again when the step closes.
options.label: Check each brief's done check
options.lose: One Sonnet call per brief, and one per step close.

title: Which three more places should get an agent that argues back?
why: All three: they're ranked by the harm each prevents, a first.
